summary: A brief list of RFCs through mid-May 1971, giving a title or partial title with its NIC and RFC numbers. It was a lookup aid for finding documents. It was replaced by later RFC lists, RFC 200 and RFC 999.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 160 is a brief list of RFCs through number 160. It pairs document titles with RFC and NIC numbers so readers could locate a note.

subtitle: A May 1971 index lists early RFC titles alongside NIC catalog numbers.

tldr.problem: Readers needed a way to find a Network Working Group note by its RFC number or title.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 160 lists titles or partial titles and gives a NIC catalog number beside each RFC number, covering entries through RFC 160.
tldr.outcome: The list records issued and unissued number slots in May 1971. It was later obsoleted by RFC 200 and RFC 999, according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 160 is historic and was obsoleted by RFCs 200 and 999. It remains a snapshot of RFC titles and NIC numbers as of May 1971.

sections.title: A Brief List of RFCs
sections.content: RFC 160 is a four-page RFC Brief List dated May 18, 1971. It gives a title or partial title, a NIC number, and an RFC number. Some numbers are explicitly marked as having no RFC issued under them.
sections.plainLanguage: The list lets readers look up an early RFC by its title or number. It also includes the NIC catalog number used to identify the document.

sections.title: What the List Contains
sections.content: The entries begin at RFC 1 and continue through RFC 160. The titles cover technical notes, meeting reports, protocol proposals, and administrative material. The list notes some RFC numbers that had not been issued or were not yet issued.
sections.plainLanguage: The list covers many kinds of network documents, not just protocol specifications. It marks some number slots that had no issued RFC.

sections.title: Later RFC Lists
sections.content: RFC 160 is itself included as the final listed entry. The unit metadata records RFCs 200 and 999 as later documents that obsoleted it, reflecting the continued replacement of early lists as the RFC collection changed.
sections.plainLanguage: This list was a snapshot of the RFC collection at that time. Later RFC lists replaced it.
